title_en: Beijing Huaqi Multimedia Production Co., Ltd. and China Audio-Video Publishing General Corporation v. Shandong Television Station — copyright infringement dispute
keywords_en: civil; copyright infringement dispute; second instance; intermediate people's court; Beijing; Shandong Province; legal person; Copyright Law; satellite television broadcast right license; validity of broadcast right transfer contract; TV station's duty to review; affirm the original judgment; TV series broadcast; satellite television transmission; broadcast right transfer; copyright; Shandong TV station copyright infringement dispute
full_text_en:
Beijing Huaqi Multimedia Production Co., Ltd. and China Audio-Visual Publishing General Office v. Shandong Television Station — dispute over copyright infringement

Plaintiffs: Beijing Huaqi Multimedia Production Co., Ltd.
Legal Representative: Dai Lu, Chairman of the Board

Plaintiffs: China Audio-Visual Publishing General Office
Legal Representative: Wang Xiaoran, Deputy Director (no chief director)

Agent ad litem for the two plaintiffs: Li Dazhong, lawyer at Beijing Long'an Law Firm

Defendant: Shandong Television Station
Legal Representative: Zeng Zhaoming, Station Director

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jinghui, Li Junsheng, staff members of Shandong Television Station

The plaintiffs, Beijing Huaqi Multimedia Production Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaqi Company) and China Audio-Visual Publishing General Office (hereinafter referred to as CAGO), filed a lawsuit with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing against the defendant, Shandong Television Station, due to a copyright dispute.

The two plaintiffs alleged: The two plaintiffs are the producers of the TV series "Waiting All the Way" (hereinafter referred to as the "Series"), and they own the copyright to the Series in accordance with the law. The defendant, Shandong Television Station, without the plaintiffs' permission, broadcast the Series to Mainland China and Asia via satellite transmission. This act of the defendant seriously infringed upon the plaintiffs' copyright, and the infringement is irreversible. The plaintiffs requested the court to order the defendant to cease the infringement, make a public apology, and compensate for economic losses of RMB 780,000.

The defendant, Shandong Television Station, argued: The Series was obtained by Shandong Hongzhi Advertising Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongzhi Company) from Hangzhou Fulaite Advertising Creative Center (hereinafter referred to as Creative Center) through Beihai Dazhong TV Culture and Art Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Dazhong Company), which granted the broadcast rights in the Shandong region. Hongzhi Company then signed a contract with the defendant to broadcast the Series on the defendant's station. When signing the contract, the defendant examined Hongzhi Company's broadcast rights and stipulated in the contract the responsibility for copyright liability. Therefore, the defendant broadcast the Series under lawful authorization, not as a pirated broadcast, and did not infringe upon the plaintiffs' rights. The defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiffs' claims.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing found the following facts upon trial:

The plaintiff CAGO holds a TV drama production license issued by the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television. On February 8, 1995, CAGO and the plaintiff Huaqi Company signed a contract for joint production of the Series. The contract stipulated: The funding for shooting the Series was to be provided by Huaqi Company, necessary documents were to be provided by CAGO, and the copyright was to be jointly owned by both parties. The television work of the Series should bear the text "Co-produced by China Audio-Visual Publishing General Office and Beijing Huaqi Multimedia Production Co., Ltd." and should include a statement: "The copyright of the literary works, audio-visual works, and musical works in this TV drama is owned by the copyright owner. No use without permission." Huaqi Company was responsible for handling the licensing of TV broadcast rights for the Series. The revenue from TV broadcast rights, after deducting the production costs invested by Huaqi Company, was to be shared between the parties, with 20% to CAGO and 80% to Huaqi Company.

On April 24, 1996, after the completion of the Series' production, the plaintiff Huaqi Company signed a paid transfer contract with the Creative Center regarding the broadcast rights of the Series. The contract stipulated: Huaqi Company (Party A) agreed to transfer the exclusive terrestrial wireless TV (non-satellite) broadcast rights of the Series within the mainland of the People's Republic of China to the Creative Center (Party B) for a price of RMB 3.4 million, valid for two years from the date of contract signing. Party B guaranteed to broadcast only within the authorized scope, not to broadcast on media outside the authorized scope, not to produce audio-visual products or publish books, and not to alter the Series tapes provided by Party A without authorization. In case of breach, Party B would bear legal liability and pay liquidated damages of RMB 5 million to Party A. During the contract period, Party A might not transfer the rights already transferred to Party B to any third party; in case of breach, Party A would refund the amount paid by Party B and compensate Party B for economic losses. Regarding the satellite TV broadcast rights of the Series, neither Huaqi Company nor the plaintiff CAGO had transferred them to others.

On August 16, 1996, the Editorial Office of the defendant Shandong Television Station (Party B) signed a contract with Hongzhi Company (Party A). The contract stipulated: Party A purchased the broadcast rights of the 25-episode TV series "Waiting All the Way" from Dazhong Company for broadcast on TV stations in the Shandong region, and agreed that the series would be broadcast on Party B's station (satellite TV station) (appended with the purchase broadcast rights contract). Party B agreed that Party A could attach commercials to be broadcast with each episode, and Party A would not charge a program fee. Party B must schedule the TV series for broadcast on the satellite TV station after February 1997. If any issues arose regarding the broadcast rights during the broadcast of this film, the responsible party would bear full liability. A 90-second commercial was to be broadcast at the beginning of each episode before the series, the content of which was to be separately agreed upon orally between the parties. When signing the contract, Shandong Television Station examined the copy of CAGO's TV drama production license provided by Hongzhi Company and a certificate issued by the Creative Center stating: "The Series is copyrighted by the Creative Center, and the Creative Center and Dazhong Company jointly distribute it." From March 16 to March 31, 1997, Shandong Television Station's satellite program broadcast the entire Series daily at approximately 22:00, preceded by a 90-second commercial. This program schedule was published in the "China TV Guide" on the corresponding dates. During the litigation, Shandong Television Station was unable to provide Hongzhi Company's purchase broadcast rights contract and its legal entity registration certificate. Upon investigation, Shandong Television Station's satellite TV program used the 10B transponder on the Asia-Pacific 1A satellite, with a downlink center frequency of 4100 Hz.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: CAGO's TV drama production license, the contract between CAGO and Huaqi Company, the contract between Huaqi Company and the Creative Center, the China TV Guide, Shandong Television Station's TV advertising broadcast instructions, the 1997 Shandong Satellite TV Channel advertising revenue table, the contract between Shandong Television Station and Hongzhi Company, the cooperative distribution certificate, the document from the ministry department of the Ministry of Radio, Film and Television, the Asia-Pacific 1A satellite coverage map, inquiry records, investigation records, and court trial records.

The Haidian District People's Court of Beijing held: The Series jointly produced by the plaintiff CAGO and the plaintiff Huaqi Company complied with the national regulations on TV drama production. Pursuant to Article 15 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Copyright Law), CAGO and Huaqi Company, as the producers of this television work, enjoy the copyright rights other than the right of authorship. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Copyright Law, other television stations that broadcast the television work of the Series must obtain permission from CAGO and Huaqi Company and pay remuneration. The defendant, Shandong Television Station, broadcast the Series on its satellite TV program without permission, thereby infringing upon the copyright of CAGO and Huaqi Company. Although Shandong Television Station held an authorized broadcast contract signed with Hongzhi Company, there was no evidence that Hongzhi Company had satellite TV broadcast rights to the Series. The certificate provided by Shandong Television Station regarding the cooperative distribution of the Series by the Creative Center and Dazhong Company was issued by the Creative Center, an interested party. This certificate could not demonstrate that the Creative Center held the copyright to the Series. Shandong Television Station failed to fulfill its duty of examination and, relying solely on this certificate, broadcast the entire Series on its nationwide satellite TV program, causing irreversible loss to the copyright owners' right to license satellite TV broadcast to others and obtain corresponding revenue. Shandong Television Station was clearly at fault. Pursuant to Article 45 of the Copyright Law, it should bear the responsibility of ceasing the broadcast, making an apology, and compensating the copyright owners with the profits obtained from the infringing broadcast. Accordingly, the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing rendered the following judgment on December 18, 1997:

1. Within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, Shandong Television Station shall make a public apology to CAGO and Huaqi Company in the "China TV Guide", and the content of the apology shall be reviewed by this court;

2. Shandong Television Station shall not broadcast the TV series "Waiting All the Way" in any form without the permission of CAGO and Huaqi Company;

3. Within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, Shandong Television Station shall compensate CAGO and Huaqi Company for economic losses of RMB 780,000.

After the first instance judgment, Shandong Television Station refused to accept it and appealed to the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court. The reasons were: 1. The appellant believed that a TV station could obtain broadcast rights not only from the copyright owner but also from the copyright owner's agent. This case involved a series of broadcast rights transfer contracts, and the Creative Center, Dazhong Company, and Hongzhi Company should be added as co-defendants. The first instance court did not conduct a comprehensive trial of these indivisible legal relationships and rashly found the appellant liable for infringement, which was based on unclear facts and insufficient evidence. 2. Before signing the contract with Hongzhi Company, the appellant had fulfilled its duty of examination and did not have subjective intention or negligence to infringe. According to Article 106 of the General Principles of Civil Law, it should not bear any liability. 3. The contract between the appellant and Hongzhi Company stipulated that the appellant's broadcast condition was to attach Hongzhi Company's commercials with the episodes, and the appellant did not obtain RMB 780,000 from Hongzhi Company. The first instance judgment ordering the appellant to bear RMB 780,000 in losses to the appellees was obviously improper. The appellant requested the court to reverse the original judgment and remand for retrial or amend the judgment.

In the second instance, the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court added Hongzhi Company as a third party in the case. Upon trial, it held that, pursuant to Article 44 of the Copyright Law, a television station that broadcasts others' films, TV programs, and video recordings must obtain permission from the film and TV program producers and video producers. Although a television station could obtain broadcast permission from an agent, it was obliged to understand the process by which the agent obtained the agency rights and the scope of agency authority. Both the appellant, Shandong Television Station, and the third party, Hongzhi Company, were insufficiently careful in this regard when signing the contract, leading to infringement, and they should bear infringement liability in accordance with the law. On this basis, and pursuant to Article 85 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court mediated the parties, and on August 27, 1998, they voluntarily reached the following settlement agreement:

Hongzhi Company shall pay RMB 720,000 to Huaqi Company and CAGO.

This mediation agreement has been executed.
